title: Out of memory after data growth
story: Batch size grows from 60 to 180 MiB after 20 s; the 128 MiB limit OOM-kills every job. Expected heal: raise memory.

timeline.thought: Dry run passed with no guardrail violations. Applying the fix now.

args.summary: Raised worker memory limit from 128m to 384m to accommodate the 180 MiB batch jobs (per job plan) that were triggering repeated OOM kills (rss 131-147 MiB > 128 MiB limit).

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: The worker's job plan steps up batch size from 60 MiB to 180 MiB at t=20s ("loading batch (180 MiB)"), and the container's 128 MiB memory limit (mem_limit_mb: 128.0) was repeatedly exceeded — logs show "Killed process ... (rss 138/144/147/144/131 MiB > limit 128 MiB)" with exit_code 137 and oom_killed:true across 4 restarts in under 2 seconds, while CPU usage stayed trivial (avg 1.6%, peak 5.0%), ruling out a CPU-related cause.
CHANGE: Raised the worker's memory limit from 128m to 384m (set_memory), giving headroom above the observed ~147 MiB peak rss for the 180 MiB batch plus process overhead, while keeping replicas at 1 as required (stateful: false but max_replicas: 1, jobs not partitioned).
GUARDRAILS: Within policy — allowed_actions includes set_memory only (respected), new memory 384m ≤ max_memory 512m, total memory 384m ≤ max_total_memory 1g, replicas unchanged at 1 (min=max=1); dry-run validation returned ok:true with no violations.
FOLLOW-UP: Monitor the next few nightly runs for further OOMs as batch sizes "grow with customer data" per watchdock.md notes — if batches exceed ~300 MiB regularly, consider a code-level batch-size cap or streaming/chunked processing rather than repeatedly raising the memory ceiling.

timeline.note: watching for 30 s with no crash or OOM
